slides.text: Every evening at exactly 6:15, an elderly man sat alone on the same railway platform with two paper cups of tea. One cup always went cold. For three years, commuters watched him smile at the empty seat beside him, quietly talking as trains arrived and departed. Nobody ever had the courage to ask who he was waiting for.

One rainy evening I finally sat beside him. He offered me the untouched cup. 'My wife was always late,' he laughed. 'Even on our first date she kept me waiting forty minutes.' I gently reminded him that she had passed away years ago. He nodded. 'I know. But if she ever decides to be late coming back, I don't want her to find me missing.'

The next week the platform was empty. The station master quietly collected two unused paper cups from the bench and placed a small handwritten note where the old man always sat. It read, 'She apologized for being late. I told her I'd already forgiven her. See you all someday — and don't leave before the people you love arrive.'
